The simulated system is subjected to an applied tensile stress of 200 MPa.
After 54,000 seconds of creep time, the γ' precipitate is rafted in the horizontal direction with an aspect ratio of 1.35.
The calculated interface energy is 0.036 J/m^2, and the interface region is discretized by 6 grid points.
The material parameters correspond to a temperature range of 1253-1293 K.
The γ/γ' misfit strain is -0.003, and the elastic stiffness constants are C11 = 198 GPa, C12 = 138 GPa, and C44 = 97 GPa.
The dislocation drag coefficient B is 10^-13 GPa·s.
The dimensionless parameter D governing the back stress is 0.6.
The Taylor factor a used in the yield stress calculation is 0.4.
The interface dislocation density typically increases from about 1 × 10^13 m^-2 up to 3-30 × 10^13 m^-2 in experiments.
The simulated interface dislocation density of around 5 × 10^13 m^-2 is in good agreement with experimental data.
Positive dislocations accumulate at the lower horizontal γ/γ' interface, while negative dislocations accumulate at the upper horizontal interface.
No significant GND accumulation is observed in the vertical channels, indicating the presence of statistically stored dislocations.
The presence of dislocations reduces the maximum long-range shear stress compared to the system without dislocations.
The plastic strain increases rapidly at first due to fast dislocation motion, then saturates as the dislocations are slowed down within the γ/γ' interfaces.
Without dislocations, the plastic strain increases linearly, which is not observed in experiments.
